title: BeaconGNN: Large-Scale GNN Acceleration with Out-of-Order Streaming In-Storage Computing
problem: Existing in-storage computing for GNN acceleration enforces strict serialized neighbor sampling that wastes flash parallelism, generates I/O requests smaller than flash access granularity causing bandwidth waste, and relies on firmware-based processing that bottlenecks backend throughput.
motivation: Graph neural networks require efficient acceleration for large-scale graph processing, and storage-level optimization is critical to meet performance demands without external bandwidth limitations.
method: BeaconGNN deploys a novel graph format enabling out-of-order neighbor sampling and near-data processing engines across multiple flash hierarchy levels (controller, channel, die). Flash-die-level samplers perform neighbor sampling while reducing channel transfers, channel-level command routers bypass firmware, and a spatial accelerator on the device bus handles GNN computation.
key_novelty: Out-of-order GNN neighbor sampling via specialized graph format combined with multi-level near-data processing across the flash storage hierarchy to eliminate firmware bottlenecks and exploit flash parallelism.
contributions: Novel graph format enabling out-of-order GNN neighbor sampling to improve flash resource utilization
Multi-level near-data processing engines deployed across controller, channel, and die hierarchy
Flash-die-level samplers that perform neighbor sampling while reducing channel transfer overhead
Spatial accelerator attached to device bus for GNN computation
baselines: Prior ISC designs for GNN acceleration
primary_theme: In-storage GNN acceleration via out-of-order sampling and multi-level near-data processing
